reports.title: National Accounts Estimates (Economic and Social Indicators)
reports.description: Statistics Mauritius's recurring national-accounts bulletin. Issue No. 1937, National Accounts Estimates, June 2026 (released 30 June 2026), covers 2023–2026. Directly verified: 'Concepts and definitions used in the computation of estimates in this issue are given at section 6.3 and are according to the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008 manual.' The same issue states the forthcoming September 2026 benchmarking (CEA 2023) 'will incorporate some of the recommendations of the System of National Accounts 2025 (SNA 2025)' — so SNA 2008 is the current compilation standard, not a legacy claim. Historical series on the Statistics Mauritius national-accounts page are labelled 'Based on 2018 CEA, 2008 SNA and NSIC Rev.2'. Cadence: quarterly ESI estimates plus an annual Digest.
reports.cadence_note: ESI National Accounts Estimates issued March/June/September/December; annual Digest of National Accounts in addition. Quarterly is the finest countable cycle.
reports._url_evidence: Fetched Statistics Mauritius ESI Issue No. 1937 PDF. Title page: National Accounts Estimates, June 2026 issue, released Tuesday 30 June 2026. SNA 2008 sentence is in the introduction of the same PDF. Subject landing page https://statsmauritius.govmu.org/Pages/Statistics/By_Subject/National_Accounts/SB_National_Accounts.aspx lists the June 2026 issue and historical QNA series tagged 2008 SNA.
reports._notes: This is the missing Mauritius national-accounts node that blocked the held-out SNA-2008 edge. Do not treat the 2011 Digest (which said SNA 2008 'has been published but not yet implemented') as current methodology.

dependencies.basis: Statistics Mauritius, National Accounts Estimates, June 2026 issue (ESI No. 1937), introduction: "Concepts and definitions used in the computation of estimates in this issue are given at section 6.3 and are according to the United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008 manual." Same bulletin notes that the next (September 2026) issue will begin incorporating some SNA 2025 recommendations after the CEA 2023 benchmark — confirming SNA 2008 is the standard of the current published series.

Statistics Mauritius National Summary Data Page (last updated 18 August 2026): "The data shown on this page correspond to the data described on the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board (DSBB). Mauritius has completed the requirements for adherence to the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) Plus, the highest tier of the Data Standards Initiatives." National Accounts is the first Real Sector row on that NSDP, sourced to Statistics Mauritius. IMF Press Release No. 26/077 (16 March 2026) states Mauritius adhered to SDDS Plus on that date, first in Africa.

Same Statistics Mauritius NSDP lists Consumer Price Index as an SDDS Plus Real Sector category (Excel/SDMX + metadata), sourced to Statistics Mauritius. The office's own 18 March 2026 communiqué: "On 16 March 2026, Mauritius has adhered to the IMF’s Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) Plus… Mauritius had subscribed to the SDDS on 28 February 2012." CPI is a prescribed SDDS/SDDS Plus price-index category already compiled monthly by this same office (ESI CPI series already in corpus).

IMF DSBB e-GDDS DQAF page for Iraq, category Balance of Payments (dsbb.imf.org/egdds/dqaf-base/country/IRQ/category/BOP00). Classification: "Transactions are classified largely in accordance with BPM6." The same page is Iraq's e-GDDS metadata for the external-accounts category (metadata first posted 15 December 2009 per the DSBB important-dates table). This is a category-level methodology statement on the e-GDDS board, not merely the dated participation row.

IMF DSBB e-GDDS DQAF page for Iran, National Accounts (GDP), last updated 6 August 2012 (the same date Iran's metadata were first posted). Verbatim: "The Central Bank of Iran (CBI) compiles and publishes Iran’s national accounts statistics. These national accounts are based on the United Nations, System of National Accounts (SNA 1968 and 1993)." This documents the e-GDDS metadata describing the live CBI national-accounts series already minted as ir-national-accounts. It is NOT an SNA-2008 claim — see _dropped.

ADDENDUM to the existing DSBB-row edge (do not mint a second parallel edge if 5s already wired af-national-accounts or af-nsia → imf-e-gdds). Corroboration from IMF Country Report No. 06/251 (July 2006), Attachment II / MEFP: "On macroeconomic statistics, in addition to the aforementioned efforts aimed at enhancing balance of payments data, we continue to make progress in drafting the metadata necessary to participate in the General Data Dissemination System." Executive Director statement in the same CR package: "In September 2004, with the assistance of international agencies, the authorities launched a statistics master plan to produce official statistics in line with international standards. Their efforts have borne fruits, and it is heartening to note that STA has indicated (since the publication of the staff report) that Afghanistan will imminently become a participant in the General Data Dissemination Standards (GDDS)." DSBB important-dates table records Afghanistan metadata first posted 22 June 2006 — the same month as the Board discussion of CR 06/251. Separate DSBB NA metadata (still SNA 1993, not 2008): "Currently, the national accounts estimates broadly follow the concepts, definitions, and classifications of the System of National Accounts 1993 (SNA 1993), as the basic data availability permit."

Da Afghanistan Bank External Sector Statistics page hosts files titled "Balance of Payments Transactions (BPM6)" and "Net International Investment Position" (latest posted edition Q1 2021; series dormant thereafter). CR 06/251 MEFP paragraph on data issues commits DAB/MoF to BOP improvement as part of the same GDDS-metadata workstream. The BPM6 labelling is DAB's own series title on dab.gov.af, not a third-party scorecard.

_dropped.why: Digest of National Accounts 2011 explicitly says "An updated version, the SNA 2008 has been published but not yet implemented" and documents 1993 SNA practice. That quote would have been the wrong-year trap for this edge. Current 2026 ESI is the verified SNA-2008 source used above.

Afghanistan DSBB NA metadata and the UN National Accounts questionnaire reply both state SNA 1993 (with residual 1968 SNA practice). No Afghan official document found this round that says the current NSIA/CSO accounts are compiled to 2008 SNA. Do not force-link to sna-2008.

Iran's own e-GDDS NA metadata (CBI): accounts "are based on the United Nations, System of National Accounts (SNA 1968 and 1993)." An older SCI methodological note likewise says 1993 SNA. Academic land-valuation papers invoking SNA 2008 for Iran are not SCI/CBI publications and do not satisfy the branch sourcing rule.

Iraq e-GDDS NA metadata (last updated 22 August 2016) states the accounts "are estimated in accordance with the concepts and methodological framework of the 1968 System of National Accounts (1968 SNA)," with only a plan "Extended adoption of the 1993 SNA, and transferring to adopt 2008 SNA." A COSIT training paper and an ESCWA note describe attempted 2008 SNA implementation, but the live DSBB metadata still records 1968 SNA. Not force-linked.

DSBB Iraq BOP metadata does say "Transactions are classified largely in accordance with BPM6," and DAB Afghanistan literally titles files BPM6. A new imf-bpm6 standards node would be the clean analogue of sna-2008, but it is not in the live international-id list reused in 5s (imf-sdds / imf-sdds-plus / imf-e-gdds / sna-2008). Not minted here; the Iraq BOP edge is instead landed on the existing imf-e-gdds metadata page that carries the BPM6 sentence. Flag for a future standards-node round if Thomas wants BPM6 as a first-class target.

Stats SL April 2026 CPI press release and the CPI Technical Methodological Guide confirm Modified Laspeyres + UN COICOP (guide: "StatsSL uses the United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) 2018 manual"). The guide's phrase "like most countries in the ECOWAS" is a comparison, not a citation of an ECOWAS instrument — same near-miss already logged in af-sierra-leone.json _dropped. No un-coicop node exists in the 5s international set. Left unlinked.
Re-checked this round against the attached Sudan slice. Membership and Article 140 remain true; still no CBS/CBOS CPI document that names COMESA or the treaty. Do not relitigate the 2026-08-13 drop.
